papers.title: Target Trial Framework: A Solution for Limited Randomized Clinical Trials in Dialysis Vascular Access?
papers.one_line: An editorial on a nationwide Australian emulation of catheter rewiring versus removal and replacement, in which 6400 patients and 9974 catheters reduce to a 434-patient emulation cohort and the label of emulation is offered as the reason to accept the result.
papers.what_was_done: The emulation under discussion drew on prospective observational data from a nationwide Australian dialysis catheter study covering 6400 patients and 9974 central venous catheters across 35 centres. Of these, 945 catheters required replacement for mechanical dysfunction, 539 by rewiring and 406 by removal and replacement, and the emulation cohort for the treatment comparison was 434 patients. Overlap weights and inverse probability of censoring weights were used to compare complication-free catheter survival, which was similar between strategies in unadjusted and adjusted analyses at one, six and twelve months, and catheter-related bloodstream infection rates were 4 percent against 6 percent. Practice varied from zero to 100 percent rewiring across the 35 centres. Fibrin sheath, a principal cause of late catheter dysfunction and the condition under which rewiring is known to fail, was not measured. Catheter tip design and the indication for fibrin sheath disruption were likewise outside the contrast, so the estimate covers rewiring against replacement as broad categories.

future_research.gap: Whether the strategies are even available at a given centre depends on local skill and equipment, which is not part of the emulated contrast
future_research.quote: The skill and hardware for ﬁbrin sheath stripping or angioplasty may only be present at some centers, and this could be a limiting factor for catheter exchange over replacement.

problems.evidence: Rewiring and removal-and-replacement are each treated as a single strategy, yet catheter tip design and whether a fibrin sheath was disrupted before reinsertion are named as the factors that determine long-term patency. Rewiring without sheath disruption is described elsewhere in the same editorial as invariably ineffective, so the two versions of rewiring differ in expected effect while sharing one arm of a 434-patient contrast, and no procedure is offered for deciding which versions belong together.
problems.quote: While the emulation trial answers a broad question of whether to rewire versus remove and replace a dysfunctional CVC, it provides limited evidence of the effect of CVC tip design or indication/s for ﬁbrin sheath disruption because these may affect the long-term patency of CVC.

problems.evidence: Across the 35 contributing centres the rewiring proportion runs from zero to 100 percent according to provider preference. A centre that never rewires contributes only to the replacement arm and a centre that always rewires only to the other, so the pooled estimate averages over sites whose emulated trials had no overlap at all, and nothing in the reported analysis distinguishes between-site from within-site contrast.
problems.quote: The type of intervention was variable across 35 centers from zero rewiring to 100% rewiring and a variable of mix of both strategies as per provider preference.

problems.evidence: A nationwide cohort of 6400 patients and 9974 catheters supports a treatment comparison in 434 patients after restriction to mechanical dysfunction and predefined exclusions, a reduction of more than 90 percent before weighting is applied. The infection comparison of 4 percent against 6 percent is then drawn from that residue, and the editorial treats the scale of the source data as the reason the question could be answered at all.
problems.quote: a target trial emulation cohort of 434 patients was selected with a predeﬁned exclusion criteria for aim 2

problems.evidence: The reasoning offered for accepting the estimate is the design label itself: an emulation is asserted to be the closest attainable answer for a question that will not be randomized, and a robust emulation technique the best available option. No assumption is named, no diagnostic is cited, and the acknowledged absence of fibrin sheath data is set beside the label rather than weighed against it.
problems.quote: An emulation trial approach to analyze real-life data is the closest one can get to answer a clinical question that is unlikely to be studied

problems.evidence: The unmeasured confounder is named precisely: fibrin sheath, which both causes late catheter dysfunction and determines whether rewiring can succeed. It is left as an acknowledgement rather than entered into the analysis, although a clinical bedside test is described in the same editorial and could serve as a proxy or negative control. Neither a proxy, a negative control nor a validation subsample is proposed, and the effect estimate stands unadjusted for it.
problems.quote: The authors acknowledge that although the study accounts for a number of confounders, it is limited in its assessment of the presence or absence of ﬁbrin sheath, a common etiology of late mechanical CVC dysfunction.

papers.title: Target trial framework for determining the effect of changes in training load on injury risk using observational data: a methodological commentary.
papers.one_line: A methodological commentary mapping the target trial protocol onto training load and injury research that concludes the framework does not solve per-protocol estimation for single time point load changes and that no observational study in existing systematic reviews has estimated a causal effect.
papers.what_was_done: Each protocol component is worked through for a non-pharmacological, self-administered exposure. No observational study in the existing systematic reviews of load and injury has explicitly estimated a causal effect, and the acute-chronic workload ratio model that underpins current training recommendations is attributed in part to methodological artifact. Load must be defined by baseline reference, absolute against relative change, single time point against continuous intervention, and by type, frequency, intensity and duration; consistency fails when a broad exposure such as activity duration ignores intensity across different sports. Positivity fails for large relative increases, illustrated by tripling training time for someone already training eight hours a day. Interference is required to be absent although teammates share schedules, which also forces clustering by team into the analysis. Immortal time bias arises because acute load is usually measured at the end of the follow-up week, so an athlete injured on day two records a lower load than one who completes the week. The remedies proposed are planned loads for an intention-to-treat contrast, an injury lag period, cloning and censoring for categorical exposures, and marginal standardization for continuous ones. Nested overlapping trials starting on consecutive days are recommended to raise the effective sample size.

future_research.gap: Isolating one component of load, estimating intention-to-treat effects without planned training data, and estimating per-protocol effects all remain unsolved under the framework
future_research.quote: Although the target trial framework solves some of the challenges compared with current approaches, other challenges remain including isolating the effects of a single aspect of load, implementing ITT or instrumental variable analyses when planned loads are not available and limitations in estimating PP effects.

problems.evidence: The interventions considered range from an individual runner adding five kilometres to a school mandating a weekly physical education class and a governing body capping youth rugby at 90 minutes per day. The comparator for a mandate is stated as the absence of the mandate with the population choosing freely, which leaves the assignment unit unspecified: the mandate applies to a school while injury occurs in a pupil, and the commentary requires clustering by team elsewhere without resolving what the unit of assignment is for a policy.
problems.quote: A comparison for a policy mandating at least one physical education class per week might be to not have this mandate in place, allowing the population to participate in physical education as they choose.

problems.evidence: A change in load has to be specified by type of activity, frequency, intensity and duration, and the commentary states that consistency fails when a broad exposure such as added activity duration ignores intensity across different sports. It then concedes that stakeholders want general recommendations and asks researchers to balance clear treatment strategies against generalisability, which is a statement of the tension rather than a procedure for grouping versions into a defensible equivalence class.
problems.quote: Consistency is likely to be violated when there is a broad intervention, such as an increase in activity duration that does not account for intensity over a variety of sports.

problems.evidence: No interference is imposed as a requirement even though the same commentary states that participants on a team share training schedules and propensities for injury and must be clustered in the analysis, which is an admission that outcomes are not independent across athletes. Separately, cloning is workable only for a dichotomous or few-category exposure, since a continuous range of load changes would require an unbounded set of clones, so the cloning device cannot represent the dose-response strategies the field actually wants.
problems.quote: Further, there cannot be interference, where an individual’s outcome depends on another individual’s treatment.

problems.evidence: The time grid is the analysis: load is aggregated over a calendar week, and whether injuries in that same week or only in a lag window afterwards are attributed to the load determines whether immortal time bias is present. A one-week lag is offered as an example without justification, and adopting it is stated to assume that load between the end of the window and the injury is irrelevant, so the choice of grid and lag changes both the bias and the estimand with no outcome-blind rule for making it.
problems.quote: Researchers sometimes impose an injury lag period, in which only injuries occurring in a specified time window (eg, 1 week) subsequent to the load window will be attributed to that load.
problems.locator: Timing of treatment assignment and immortal time bias

problems.evidence: Eligibility is assessed on each day, so an athlete eligible on Monday and again on Tuesday contributes two overlapping week-long trials that share six days of exposure and outcome time. The stated benefit is a larger effective sample size and the stated cost is only the need to account for repeated measures; nothing addresses the calendar-time structure created when trials starting in different weeks of a season are pooled, although the commentary elsewhere notes that recovery and taper weeks systematically precede large load increases.
problems.quote: These cross-over trials can overlap within individuals.

problems.evidence: The intention-to-treat contrast requires planned loads, which are usually not collected, and the per-protocol contrast requires an unbiased measure of observed load, which the end-of-week measurement cannot provide. What is left is a different estimand defined by the available data, an effect of load measured after a lag window, and the commentary states outright that the framework does not solve per-protocol estimation for the single time point interventions athletes and coaches care about.
problems.quote: Despite the advantages of target trial emulation, it does not solve the challenge of estimating PP effects for specific single time point interventions which may be of interest to athletes, coaches and clinicians.
problems.locator: Estimating PP effects in observational data

papers.title: Prospective benchmarking of an observational analysis in the SWEDEHEART registry against the REDUCE-AMI randomized trial.
papers.one_line: A target trial emulated in SWEDEHEART registry data and published before the REDUCE-AMI trial reported, estimating a per-protocol 5-year risk difference of minus 0.8 percentage points for beta blockers with a compatibility interval from minus 4.5 to plus 2.8.
papers.what_was_done: A protocol was written to match the ongoing REDUCE-AMI trial as closely as possible and emulated in SWEDEHEART linked to the Swedish patient, cause of death and prescribed drug registers, with the trial results not yet available. Of the eligible individuals, 10 926 entered the emulation, 9728 assigned to beta blockers and 1198 to no beta blockers, and assignment was defined by a beta blocker prescription within 30 days of angiography. Adjustment used inverse probability weights over roughly 40 baseline covariates, and time-varying weights adjusted for censoring at non-adherence in the per-protocol analysis. The intention-to-treat 5-year risks of death or myocardial infarction were 10.2 percent with 95 percent CI 9.4 to 11.1 under beta blockers and 11.9 percent with 95 percent CI 8.5 to 15.3 under no beta blockers, giving a risk difference of minus 1.7 percentage points with 95 percent CI minus 5.5 to 1.9; the per-protocol risk difference was minus 0.8 with 95 percent CI minus 4.5 to 2.8. Adherence was 74 percent in the beta blocker group and 91 percent in the no beta blocker group. Average hazard ratios were also reported at three, four and five years. The trial protocol supplies no adherence definition and no explicit exclusion for prior beta blocker use, so both were invented for the emulation.

future_research.gap: Whether population composition rather than treatment effect explains any discrepancy between the trial and the emulation is not resolved in advance
future_research.quote: Subgroup analyses may be needed to understand if a different composition of the study populations explains different effect estimates between the index trial and the target trial emulation.

future_research.gap: Prognostic factors for non-adherence are not observed between hospital visits, leaving the per-protocol estimate open to residual bias
future_research.quote: This could be a source of residual bias in our per protocol analyses.

problems.evidence: The declared purpose of the benchmark is to license further questions: if the emulation reproduces REDUCE-AMI, the same registry and the same analytic machinery are to be trusted for questions the trial could not answer. No argument is given for why agreement on the effect of long-term beta blockade after myocardial infarction with preserved ejection fraction would transfer to a different treatment, comparator or outcome in the same data, and the risk difference at stake is minus 0.8 percentage points inside an interval from minus 4.5 to plus 2.8, which most trial results would be compatible with.
problems.quote: If this prospective benchmarking is successful, it supports the credibility of additional analyses using these observational data, which can rapidly deliver answers to questions that could not be answered by the initial trial.

problems.evidence: Publishing the emulation before the trial reports removes the possibility of tuning the analysis to a known answer, and the plan names the comparisons that will be made: risk differences and risk ratios at five years and a harmonized per-protocol contrast rather than the hazard ratio alone. What remains open is the verdict itself. Success and failure are still binary labels with no pre-specified tolerance on the risk difference, and the response to disagreement is an unspecified postmortem rather than a calibrated statement of how far apart the two estimands were.
problems.quote: If benchmarking proves unsuccessful, we will conduct a “postmortem” analysis to identify the reasons for the discrepancy.

problems.evidence: The trial being benchmarked against does not define adherence, so the emulation invents one: a gap of less than 180 days between the end of one dispensation and the next. Daily dose is likewise assumed at 100 mg metoprolol and 5 mg bisoprolol because the register records dose correctly only for the primary indication. The per-protocol estimand is therefore defined by these two data-driven choices rather than by the protocol, and a sensitivity analysis tightening the gap to 90 days is reported as a robustness check rather than as evidence that a different estimand was being estimated.
problems.quote: The REDUCE-AMI protocol does not specify a definition of adherence, so we proposed the definition of adherence to be a gap of less than 180 days between the end date of one dispensation and the following dispensation
problems.locator: The observational emulation of the target trial

problems.evidence: The trial criterion excludes anyone with an indication for beta blockers other than secondary prevention according to the treating physician, which is a clinical judgment that leaves no trace in a register. The emulation substitutes exclusion of any prior beta blocker use in the previous three years plus a list of proxy characteristics, and when the prior-use exclusion is relaxed in sensitivity analysis the five-year risks rise in both arms and the effect estimate attenuates. An unrecorded judgment is thus indistinguishable from its absence and the substitute criterion measurably moves the answer.
problems.quote: Second, the target trial emulation cannot fully replicate eligibility criteria that are vaguely articulated for the index trial.

problems.evidence: Baseline is extended to 30 days after angiography because community prescribing is common after discharge, which is a grace period chosen for administrative convenience rather than by an outcome-blind rule. Individuals with an event in those 30 days are excluded, and the misalignment this creates is checked afterwards with a cloning and censoring sensitivity analysis. The 30-day window, the 180-day adherence gap and the five-year horizon are all set before the analysis but none is selected by a stated procedure that could have chosen otherwise.
problems.quote: Eligible individuals were “assigned” to the beta blocker group if they received a prescription of beta blockers within 30 days of angiography
problems.locator: The observational emulation of the target trial

problems.evidence: The comparator arm holds 1198 individuals against 9728 in the treated arm, so 11 percent of the cohort supports the entire counterfactual for no beta blockers, and the estimated 5-year risk in that arm carries an interval from 8.5 to 15.3 percent against 9.4 to 11.1 in the treated arm. Weighting proceeds over roughly 40 baseline covariates with no report of which covariate histories among the no-treatment arm have no treated counterpart, and no positivity diagnostic beyond the width of the resulting intervals.
problems.quote: Compared with those assigned to no beta blockers (1,198 individuals), those assigned to beta blockers (9,728 individuals) were, on average, younger, and more likely to smoke

papers.title: Combining high quality data with rigorous methods: emulation of a target trial using electronic health records and a nested case-control design.
papers.one_line: A nested case-control emulation of a statin initiation trial in Kaiser Permanente Washington records showing that ICD-based outcome ascertainment with 95 to 96 percent sensitivity and 98 percent specificity moves the odds ratio from 0.80 to 1.00.
papers.what_was_done: A target trial of statin initiation for prevention of myocardial infarction was emulated under a nested case-control design using electronic health records from Kaiser Permanente Washington, with outcomes validated by medical record review through the Heart and Vascular Health study. Of 10 128 unique cases and controls, 1221 cases and 4267 controls met eligibility for at least one person trial, the main reason for exclusion being absent confounder data in the six months before enrollment. 198 monthly trials were created between January 1994 and June 2010, generating 15 263 eligible case person trials and 76 315 sampled control person trials at five controls per case. Statin treatment was initiated in 1.9 percent of case person trials and 1.5 percent of control person trials. The intention-to-treat odds ratio was 1.26 with 95 percent CI 1.10 to 1.44 before confounder adjustment and 0.80 with 95 percent CI 0.69 to 0.92 after, against a pooled hazard ratio of 0.69 from a meta-analysis of trials. The per-protocol odds ratio was 0.71 with 95 percent CI 0.58 to 0.87 with weights truncated at 2.4. Repeating the analysis with unvalidated ICD-based cases and controls gave 1.00 with 95 percent CI 0.90 to 1.10, and a conventional case-control analysis measuring covariates at the index date gave 1.12.

future_research.gap: Existing case-control studies with covariates measured only at the index date cannot be reanalyzed by this method
future_research.quote: Therefore, such analyses cannot be implemented within existing case-control studies that have measured such factors only at the index date
future_research.locator: Strengths and limitations of this study

problems.evidence: This supplies the measurement the entry asks for: outcome phenotype accuracy of 95 to 96 percent sensitivity and 98 percent specificity against medical record review, and the resulting bias quantified by running the same emulation both ways, giving 0.80 with validation and 1.00 without. What it does not close is the general case. Validation covers the outcome only, exposure and confounder phenotypes remain error-free binary variables, the design requires a validation subsample that most emulations do not have, and no correction is applied to the unvalidated estimate; the accuracy figures are reported after the fact rather than propagated into the interval.
problems.quote: In our clinical example, we obtained a sensitivity of 95-96% and a specificity of 98% for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction by ICD codes compared with medical reviews

problems.evidence: Among sampled controls, 8 percent of non-initiators had started statins by one year and 38 percent by five years, while 41 percent of initiators had stopped by one year and 64 percent by five. The two arms converge steadily over follow-up, and the intention-to-treat odds ratio of 0.80 sits closer to the null than the per-protocol 0.71 and further from the trial meta-analytic 0.69, exactly the attenuation the entry describes. Follow-up runs to 17 years, and no analysis reports how the intention-to-treat contrast varies with the length of follow-up.
problems.quote: Conversely, 8% (7210 of 90 124) of non-initiators started treatment within one year and 38% (34 247 of 90 124) started treatment within five years

problems.evidence: Positivity is addressed by truncating the stabilized weights at the 99th centile, a value of 2.4, and by a general statement that violations grow with follow-up length. Neither says which patient histories lacked support. With statin initiation occurring in 1.9 percent of case person trials and non-adherence weights accumulating over as much as 17 years, the truncation discards precisely the histories where the data were thinnest, and the analysis reports the weight distribution instead of the unsupported covariate patterns.
problems.quote: Such violations are more common with longer durations of follow-up and may lead to undue influence of a few observations.
problems.locator: Strengths and limitations of this study

problems.evidence: 198 monthly trials expand 1221 cases and 4267 controls into 15 263 case person trials and 76 315 control person trials, so an individual can appear dozens of times and, as the table footnote records, in both the initiator and non-initiator groups in different person trials. Trials are spread over 16 years of calendar time during which statin prescribing changed substantially, and calendar month enters only as an adjustment covariate; the efficiency gain from expansion is reported as the reason for the design while the repeated participation is handled as a variance nuisance.
problems.quote: Across all trials, 15 263 were eligible case person trials, and we sampled five controls for each case using incidence density sampling, thereby creating 76 315 control person trials

problems.evidence: The prescription for variance after sequence expansion is a single clause naming a robust variance estimator as an example, with the detail deferred to a supplementary guideline. With 76 315 control person trials drawn from 4267 individuals, time-varying weights for adherence and censoring, and truncation at 2.4, the sandwich estimator has to absorb both within-person correlation and weight estimation, and no evidence is offered that the resulting intervals of 0.69 to 0.92 and 0.58 to 0.87 have nominal coverage.
problems.quote: If each patient is allowed to enroll in multiple trials, the variance of the estimated effect size should be adjusted for the within person correlation of person trials using an appropriate variance estimator, such as a robust variance estimator.

problems.evidence: A detailed guideline, a SAS macro and a sample dataset are published as supplementary files, which is more than most emulations release and closes the code half of the entry for this design. The rest stays open: the data sharing statement declares that no additional data are available, the ICD-9 phenotype logic and the validation protocol are described in prose rather than deposited, weight diagnostics beyond the truncation point are not reported, and no record exists of the protocol versions considered and rejected during the iterative reformulation the paper describes.
problems.quote: Supplemental file 1 provides a detailed guideline and an analytical code to implement the target trial emulation approach using a nested case-control design.

papers.title: Representation of Real-World Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease in Clinical Trials Supporting Blood Pressure Treatment Targets.
papers.one_line: Applying SPRINT, ACCORD and AASK eligibility criteria to 503 480 Veterans Affairs and 73 412 Kaiser Permanente adults with chronic kidney disease and hypertension leaves only 23.8 percent and 20.8 percent trial-eligible.
papers.what_was_done: A cross-sectional analysis identified adults with chronic kidney disease, defined as eGFR below 60 sustained for at least 90 days in 2019, and hypertension, defined as an outpatient systolic pressure of 120 mm Hg or higher on two separate visits or a 90-day antihypertensive prescription with at least one outpatient measurement. The inclusion and exclusion criteria of three blood pressure target trials were operationalized against the electronic record. Of 503 480 Veterans Affairs and 73 412 Kaiser Permanente Southern California adults, 79.7 percent and 87.3 percent had a systolic pressure above the guideline target, while 23.8 percent with 95 percent CI 23.7 to 24.0 and 20.8 percent with 95 percent CI 20.5 to 21.1 met the criteria of at least one trial. Among adults with diabetes, only 10.2 percent in Veterans Affairs and 2.6 percent in Kaiser Permanente were ACCORD-eligible. Representativeness was lowest below age 50 and among Hispanic patients, and no trial covered adults with eGFR under 15. Missing laboratory values reached 28.6 percent for Veterans Affairs eligibility variables and were handled by fully conditional specification with 30 imputation sets. Certain criteria, including limited life expectancy and adherence, could not be operationalized at all, and the record does not distinguish routine office pressures from the standardized measurements the trials used.

future_research.gap: Treatment decisions for patients who develop acute kidney injury while on blood pressure lowering agents are not covered by any of the trials
future_research.quote: For example, it remains unclear whether patients should continue BP‐lowering agents if they develop acute kidney injury.

problems.evidence: Two of the trials' criteria, limited life expectancy and adherence, have no representation in the electronic record and were simply dropped from the operationalization. Every patient in the 503 480 and 73 412 denominators is therefore treated as satisfying criteria that were never assessed, which inflates the eligible fractions of 23.8 percent and 20.8 percent by an unknown amount in a direction that cannot be signed from the data.
problems.quote: Third, we were unable to operationalize certain inclusion and exclusion criteria from electronic health records, such as limited life expectancy or adherence.

problems.evidence: Both the disease definition and the hypertension definition are built from healthcare-use variables: an eGFR sustained across at least 90 days of outpatient laboratory results, and two outpatient pressure readings on separate visits in one calendar year. Patients enter the denominator only by attending often enough to be measured twice and to have creatinine drawn twice, so both the numerator and denominator of the representativeness estimate are conditioned on utilization, and the alternative definition using a 130 mm Hg threshold moves the eligible fraction from 23.8 percent to 41.5 percent.
problems.quote: We defined hypertension as the presence of an outpatient systolic BP ≥120 mm Hg on 2 separate visits during the calendar year to replicate trial screening and enrollment procedures

problems.evidence: Systolic blood pressure is the same named variable in the trials and in the two health systems, but the trials used standardized measurement protocols and the records mix those with routine office readings that cannot be separated. Since the exclusion criterion appearing most often is a systolic pressure below 130 mm Hg, the entire eligibility calculation turns on a variable whose meaning differs between the two sources, and the paper states no correction factor can be applied because the relationship between the two is too variable.
problems.quote: First, although we required >1 elevated BP measurement on separate days to define hypertension, the data set did not differentiate routine office BP from standardized BP measurements recommended by guidelines.

problems.evidence: Fewer than one in four real-world adults with chronic kidney disease and hypertension satisfy any of the three trials, and the trial samples carry higher systolic pressure, higher LDL and more ischemic heart disease while excluding those with low diastolic pressure, heart failure, dementia and cancer. Transporting a trial estimate onto the 503 480 and 73 412 populations therefore requires a sampling model on top of the trials' internal validity, and the direction of the discrepancy is the opposite for benefit and for harm, since the trials were enriched for cardiovascular risk and depleted of adverse-event risk simultaneously.
problems.quote: In other words, trials were enriched for those at high risk for cardiovascular events and at low risk for adverse treatment events compared with real‐world CKD populations.

problems.evidence: Coverage is worst in exactly the groups that most need a subgroup-specific answer: adults under 50, Hispanic adults, and those with advanced disease, with no trial covering eGFR below 15 because all three excluded it. Any emulation restricted to trial-eligible strata will therefore produce its thinnest support for the youngest, the Hispanic and the most severely affected patients, and the paper proposes emulated trials in large data sets as the remedy for precisely those gaps without noting that overlap there will be worst.
problems.quote: Trial representativeness was lowest among those <50 years of age and among those of Hispanic ethnicity
problems.locator: RESULTS, Trial Representativeness by Age, Race and Ethnicity, and eGFR

problems.evidence: The operational definitions of every inclusion and exclusion criterion for three trials, applied across two health systems and reported only in supplementary tables, are the entire substance of the result, and the code implementing them is available on request from one author rather than deposited. Nothing about the phenotype logic for chronic kidney disease, the imputation of up to 28.6 percent missing eligibility variables, or the definitions rejected along the way is recoverable by a reader.
problems.quote: The analytic code for this study is available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

papers.title: Patients on vitamin K treatment: is switching to direct-acting oral anticoagulation cost-effective? A target trial on a prospective cohort.
papers.one_line: A target trial emulation in the Swiss-AF cohort estimating the cost-effectiveness of switching from vitamin K antagonists to direct oral anticoagulants, reporting an ICER of CHF 425 852 per QALY built from survival on 791 patients, utilities on 783 and costs on 351.
papers.what_was_done: The Swiss-AF prospective cohort enrolled 2415 atrial fibrillation patients across 14 Swiss centres between 2014 and 2017, with claims linkage available for 1024 patients, or 42.4 percent of the cohort. Eligibility required at least one year of vitamin K antagonist treatment; time zero was the switch date for switchers and the date the one-year criterion was met for maintainers. Inverse probability weights from a logistic model for switching were applied to a weighted Cox model for survival and to longitudinal linear models for utilities and costs. Of 873 eligible patients, 791 entered the survival analysis, 783 had complete quality-of-life data and 351 had claims for the cost analysis. The weighted hazard ratio for all-cause survival was 0.99 with 95 percent CI 0.45 to 1.55, the utility difference was minus 0.01 with 95 percent CI minus 0.03 to 0.01, incremental costs were CHF 23 033 with 95 percent CI minus 8681 to 63 442, and the base-case ICER was CHF 425 852 per QALY gained. A conventional regression cohort analysis without a valid time zero gave a hazard ratio of 0.71 and 0.17 QALYs gained on the same data. All direct oral anticoagulants were pooled as one class and utilities between planned visits were linearly interpolated.

future_research.gap: The reasons clinicians switch anticoagulant remain unmeasured, so the weighting model cannot be shown to have removed confounding by indication
future_research.quote: Such factors might, for example, be the emergence or worsening of conditions unrelated to AF, triggering a need or wish to simplify patient management.

problems.evidence: A cohort of 2415 enrolled patients yields 873 eligible for the target trial, 791 analysable for survival and 351 for costs, so the cost arm of the primary estimand rests on 14 percent of the enrolled cohort. The consequence is visible in the intervals: incremental costs run from minus CHF 8681 to CHF 63 442, wide enough that the ICER of CHF 425 852 per QALY is uninformative about the sign of the numerator, and the paper attributes this directly to the limited number of patients with claims.
problems.quote: Of 873 eligible patients in the target trial, 791 were included in the survival analysis, 783 had complete data on QoL and 351 patients had available claims data for cost analysis.

problems.evidence: Dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban and edoxaban are collapsed into a single treatment arm, and the stated justification is statistical power and the fact that all are available in routine practice. No argument establishes that these four agents form a clinically defensible equivalence class for either the survival or the cost outcome, and drug-specific costs differ enough to matter for a CHF 425 852 per QALY ratio in which average annual DOAC cost is roughly CHF 1000 against CHF 80 for vitamin K antagonists.
problems.quote: Second, we treated all DOAC drugs as a class, not distinguishing the different drugs and their respective effects on clinical outcomes.

problems.evidence: Utilities exist only at planned yearly study visits and the values in between are filled in by linear interpolation, while patients with missing quality-of-life information are censored. The visit schedule therefore determines both where the outcome is observed and who leaves the analysis, and the QALY component of the ICER is a deterministic function of that schedule; no model of the visit or attendance process is fitted and no sensitivity analysis varies the interpolation rule.
problems.quote: Information on utility was only available at planned study visits, so utilities on dates between visits were assumed to follow a linear relationship.
problems.locator: Methods, Target trial and statistical analysis

problems.evidence: The same data and the same confounder set give a hazard ratio of 0.99 under the target trial emulation and 0.71 under a conventional cohort regression that sets time zero at the one-year mark for everyone, and 0.003 versus 0.17 QALYs gained. A propensity score matching alternative is reported to agree with the emulation, so the design choice rather than the estimator drives the gap, and no criterion is offered in advance for which analysis should have been believed.
problems.quote: In the conventional regression-based cohort analysis performed for comparison, the HR of overall survival was 0.71

problems.evidence: Agreement with randomized evidence is asserted as a bare claim of alignment with no comparison of estimands, no quantitative calibration and no statement of which trial estimate is being matched. The emulation targets a five-year incremental cost-effectiveness ratio in switchers with at least one year of vitamin K antagonist exposure, whereas the cited trial evidence concerns event rates in frail switchers, so the two estimands differ in population, outcome and time horizon while the reported comparison is a single word.
problems.quote: Our estimates align with results from a previous randomised trial.

problems.evidence: Time zero is the switch date in one arm and the date of meeting a one-year exposure criterion in the other, so the two arms are anchored to structurally different events and no grace period is specified within which a switch would still count as baseline. The one-year threshold, the five-year horizon and the three percent discount rate are all fixed by convention rather than by an outcome-blind procedure, and the only related sensitivity analysis excludes 24 patients who switched within one month of a clinical event.
problems.quote: For patients maintaining VKA treatment, the time point of meeting the eligibility criterion for inclusion in the trial was used, that is, being on VKA treatment for at least 1 year.
problems.locator: Methods, Target trial and statistical analysis

new_problems.proposed_title: A cost-effectiveness ratio from an emulated trial is assembled from components estimated on different subsamples with no estimand defined for the ratio
new_problems.statement: Emulations that report an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio estimate survival, utility and cost on nested but different analysis samples, under different censoring and interpolation rules, and then divide one by another; no estimand is defined for the resulting ratio and no procedure propagates the differing identification assumptions of its components.
new_problems.why_open: In this emulation the survival model used 791 patients, the utility model 783 and the cost model 351, the last being the subset with claims linkage, and the reported ICER of CHF 425 852 per QALY is the ratio of an incremental cost estimated on 351 patients to an incremental QALY estimated on 783. Uncertainty is summarized by bootstrapping the components together, but nothing states what counterfactual contrast the ratio identifies, whether the claims-linkage subsample satisfies the exchangeability condition assumed for the full cohort, or how censoring for missing quality-of-life data interacts with cost accrual. The same pattern appears in the emergency surgery emulation for health technology assessment, where quality-adjusted life-years are constructed by attaching published utility weights from other populations to administrative resource-use records.
new_problems.quote: Of 873 eligible patients in the target trial, 791 were included in the survival analysis, 783 had complete data on QoL and 351 patients had available claims data for cost analysis.
new_problems.checked_against_index: EST-03 concerns an effect measure standing in for a weighted per-protocol contrast and says nothing about ratios whose numerator and denominator are estimated on different samples. GMT-03 concerns shrinkage of the effective sample after eligibility and weighting, not the recombination of components estimated under different assumptions. PRO-01 asks for a decomposition of scientific-target mismatch, protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error, which presupposes a single defined estimand rather than a composite ratio that has none.

papers.title: Making causal inferences from transactional data: A narrative review of opportunities and challenges when implementing the target trial framework.
papers.one_line: A narrative review of target trial emulation with electronic health records and claims data that walks each protocol component through its transactional-data emulation and concludes that identifiability assumptions are seldom fully met.
papers.what_was_done: PubMed/Medline and Google Scholar were searched with terms covering causal inference, target trial, electronic medical records and insurance claims data; no counts of screened or included records are reported and no quantitative synthesis is attempted. The review restates the three identifiability assumptions and then maps each of the seven target trial protocol components onto an emulation using transactional data, naming electronic phenotyping, natural language processing of clinical notes and common data models such as OMOP as the mitigations for eligibility and outcome misclassification. It states that only pragmatic target trials can be emulated because real-world data cannot support a placebo-controlled or blinded design. Loss to follow-up is defined operationally by absence of healthcare utilization for a long enough interval, which makes the visit process part of the censoring definition. Data incompleteness is attributed to passive recording that depends on patients attending a healthcare center, and to selective recording of what a clinician judges relevant, with education, symptom severity, functional status and social determinants named as the variables most affected. No thresholds, no numeric quality criteria and no decision rule for abandoning a study are supplied at any point.

future_research.gap: Residual confounding cannot be excluded in emulations built on transactional data, and no procedure bounds its magnitude
future_research.quote: Importantly, even with rigorous methodology, residual confounding bias can never be entirely ruled out in observational studies.
future_research.locator: Interpreting results: navigating through potential biases

problems.evidence: Data fitness is handled by a single narrative instruction that an absent variable should prompt reconsideration of the study, with no threshold on completeness, no measurement of how much information is missing and no rule that would stop the study rather than trigger reformulation of the question. The review names privacy, subjectivity of recording and differential access as challenges and offers electronic phenotyping and common data models as remedies without a criterion for judging whether the remedy worked.
problems.quote: The absence of information on a relevant variable should prompt the research team to consider the usefulness of the study or the need to reformulate the target trial.
problems.locator: Components of the target trial protocol and their emulation using transactional data sources

problems.evidence: Measurement error in eligibility, exposure, outcome and confounder variables is acknowledged as pervasive in electronic health records, and the proposed responses are manual chart review, phenotype refinement and standardized extraction tools. None of these produces an error rate that enters the analysis: phenotypes are still carried into the emulation as binary variables and no correction, bound or sensitivity parameter is attached to them.
problems.quote: Eligibility criteria, exposures, outcomes, and/or confounders may be measured with error in EHR data.
problems.locator: Interpreting results: navigating through potential biases

problems.evidence: Censoring for loss to follow-up is defined by the absence of healthcare system contact for a long enough period, which makes the visit process itself the operational definition of the end of follow-up rather than a structure to be modeled. The same section notes that recording is passive and depends on patients attending a healthcare center, so patients who stop attending are simultaneously less informative and treated as censored, and no model of the visit process is proposed.
problems.quote: A frequent choice is to use the lack of appointments or utilization of the healthcare system for a significant amount of time.
problems.locator: Components of the target trial protocol and their emulation using transactional data sources

problems.evidence: The review concedes that the identifying assumptions are seldom fully met and then asks investigators to discuss sources of bias and give a general assessment of magnitude and direction in prose. Nothing separates assumptions that could be checked in the data from those that cannot, and formal sensitivity analysis is offered as an optional supplement rather than a required per-assumption report.
problems.quote: Identifiability assumptions required for causal inference are seldom fully met.
problems.locator: Interpreting results: navigating through potential biases

problems.evidence: Dynamic strategies are said to require data both on treatment received and on the circumstances excusing a patient from the assigned strategy, using myopathy or hepatic impairment during statin treatment as the example. Whether those circumstances were even assessed depends on when the patient was seen, so the excusal condition is observed on a treatment-dependent schedule; the review names the data requirement but supplies no identification result for continuous-time regimes under such observation.
problems.quote: Emulating a target trial that involves a comparison of dynamic treatment strategies requires adequate data, not only on treatment received but also on the circumstances under which patients are ‘excused’ from following the assigned treatment
problems.locator: Components of the target trial protocol and their emulation using transactional data sources

problems.evidence: An eligibility criterion built from healthcare-use variables, requiring a minimum period of enrollment or a minimum number of interactions with the system, is presented as routine practice for identifying regular users. The same review records that recording is passive and that patients with more consultations are overrepresented, so the criterion selects on a variable driven by both health status and access; no collider argument or diagnostic accompanies the recommendation.
problems.quote: For this reason, an eligibility criterion requiring a minimum time or interactions with the system is often included.
problems.locator: Components of the target trial protocol and their emulation using transactional data sources

papers.title: Emulating Target Trials With Real-World Data to Inform Health Technology Assessment: Findings and Lessons From an Application to Emergency Surgery.
papers.one_line: A target trial emulation of emergency surgery for acute appendicitis and gallstone disease in 268 144 and 240 977 English hospital admissions, in which the intention-to-treat effect could not be emulated at all and 92 percent of appendicitis patients received the index strategy.
papers.what_was_done: Hospital Episode Statistics for 2010 to 2019 linked to national mortality data were used to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of emergency surgery against non-emergency management for two acute gastrointestinal conditions, with 268 144 eligible appendicitis and 240 977 gallstone admissions. Two panels of 12 clinicians ran a modified Delphi process requiring at least 9 of 12 in favour to fix the diagnostic subcategories with equipoise, 5 for appendicitis and 3 for gallstone disease, and to designate 21 and 45 procedure codes as emergency surgery within a 7-day window from assessment. Time zero was set at the first episode under a consultant surgeon after two alternatives were rejected. Of eligible patients, 92 percent of appendicitis and 22 percent of gallstone cases met the emergency surgery definition. Local instrumental variable analysis using hospital tendency to operate gave incremental net benefit at one year of minus 86.2 pounds with 95 percent CI minus 1163 to 991 for appendicitis and 221 pounds with 95 percent CI minus 450 to 892 for gallstones, against regression estimates of minus 223 and minus 220 and unadjusted estimates of 1431 and 1002. Subgroup results indicated emergency surgery was not cost-effective for severely frail patients and those with two or more comorbidities.

future_research.gap: Benchmarking against randomized evidence is unavailable in most decision-relevant settings, so the credibility of an emulation for health technology assessment cannot be established that way
future_research.quote: Nevertheless, in many settings, RCT evidence for benchmarking is unavailable or unsuitable as it fails to include the target populations, comparators, or endpoints of decision-making relevance.

problems.evidence: One of the two causal contrasts in the protocol is simply unavailable because the administrative record holds treatment received and not treatment assignment. The study proceeds on the per-protocol contrast alone, justified by asserting that adherence to assignment is plausible in routine practice, so an unobservable protocol component silently redefines the estimand rather than adding noise to it, and the resulting net benefit figures of minus 86.2 and 221 pounds answer a question the protocol listed second.
problems.quote: ITT effect could not be emulated because information on the initial treatment assignment was not available from HES.

problems.evidence: The comparator is everything that is not one of the designated procedures inside 7 days, which mixes antibiotic management, no surgery within a year, and surgery outside the window or with a non-designated code. Antibiotic duration and dosage are absent from the data, so the contrast is against a basket rather than any defined alternative, and the paper states that no specific non-surgical strategy could be evaluated. The intervention arm is equally broad, spanning 21 and 45 procedure codes fixed by a 9 of 12 panel vote.
problems.quote: This lack of granular information meant that although the study could evaluate the cost-effectiveness of ES versus a general “basket” of NES strategies, it could not contrast with any one speciﬁc NES strategy.

problems.evidence: The grace period is fixed by an outcome-blind procedure: a Delphi panel of 12 clinicians, requiring at least 9 in favour, sets the 7-day window before any outcome is examined, and three explicit criteria are stated for time zero, with two candidates rejected against them. That is more discipline than most emulations apply. It does not close the entry. No rule maps clinical judgment to a number, the same panel that fixed the window also fixed eligibility and the intervention definition, no alternative window is examined in sensitivity analysis, and the residual bias is argued away by a claim that 7-day mortality is low rather than measured.
problems.quote: and that for both conditions the time window for ES should be within 7 days of assessment (baseline/time zero, see below).

problems.evidence: Which ICD-10 subcategories describe patients eligible for emergency surgery in routine practice is not recoverable from the data or from published evidence, so a panel vote decides. A patient whose subcategory failed to reach 9 of 12 votes is outside the 268 144 and 240 977 denominators for a reason that has nothing to do with their record, and the same mechanism excludes pregnancy and appendiceal cancer for appendicitis while excluding nothing for gallstone disease.
problems.quote: For other criteria, such as the reason for admission, the information from the routine data and the available evidence were insufﬁcient to deﬁne which patient subgroups to include.
problems.locator: Target Population for the Decision Problem

problems.evidence: Three analyses are run that differ only in what they assume about confounding: no confounding at all, all confounders measured, and unmeasured confounding handled by a local instrumental variable. They span incremental net benefit from 1431 pounds to minus 223 to minus 86.2 for appendicitis. Every other violated assumption stays fixed across the three, including the basket comparator, the panel-defined eligible population and the missing intention-to-treat contrast, so no analysis in the set varies two assumptions together.
problems.quote: For completeness we also included a naive comparison, which assumed there were no confounders.

problems.evidence: For appendicitis, 92 percent of eligible patients received emergency surgery, so the entire non-surgical counterfactual rests on 8 percent of 268 144 admissions, and the panel-defined eligibility criterion of being under a surgeon's care was chosen precisely to remove patients whose prognosis made one strategy unthinkable. No diagnostic names which case-mix profiles among that 8 percent have no surgical counterpart, and the subgroup estimates that drive the policy conclusion are reported for severe frailty and multiple comorbidity, the strata where treated and untreated counts are smallest.
problems.quote: Of these patients, 92% (appendicitis) and 22% (gallstone disease) met the deﬁnition of ES

papers.title: Development of the TrAnsparent ReportinG of observational studies Emulating a Target trial (TARGET) guideline.
papers.one_line: A protocol for a five-stage reporting guideline for target trial emulations, whose systematic review identifies eligible studies by whether they say they emulated a target trial and whose consensus meeting resolves item disputes by simple majority.
papers.what_was_done: A working group of methodologists, trialists, biostatisticians, regulators and editors plans a reporting guideline in five stages between late 2022 and early 2025. Stage 1 is a registered systematic review of MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO and Science Citation Index for observational studies stating in their methods that they explicitly emulated a target trial, with extraction covering study characteristics, whether the study was prospectively registered, and whether and how each of the seven protocol components was specified and emulated. Stage 2 runs two REDCap surveys in which working group members rate candidate items on a nine-point Likert scale from not important to critically important, with free-text responses analysed by reflexive thematic analysis. Stage 3 is a two-day consensus meeting where unresolved disagreements go to an anonymised vote decided by simple majority. Stage 4 drafts the guideline and an explanation and elaboration document and pilots them with 20 to 30 methodologists. Stage 5 covers dissemination through journals, funders and an EQUATOR listing. The stated motivation is that a template exists for specifying a target trial and its emulation but no detailed guidance exists for reporting one.

future_research.gap: No detailed reporting guidance exists for studies emulating a target trial, so appraisal and synthesis of the growing literature is currently unsupported
future_research.quote: however, there is currently no detailed guidance on reporting a study designed to emulate a target trial

problems.evidence: Inclusion in the review that will define reporting practice turns on self-description: a study qualifies by stating target trial emulation in the article, and the protocol acknowledges in the same paragraph that many observational studies use the framework implicitly and will be excluded. The corpus is therefore assembled by label rather than by any property of the design, so studies that describe themselves as emulations set the reporting standard while equally rigorous analyses that do not use the phrase are outside it.
problems.quote: However, to be included in this review studies must be explicit in their attempt to emulate a target trial (eg, stated ‘target trial emulation’ in the article).

problems.evidence: The extraction list records design characteristics, the seven protocol components as specified and emulated, and whether the study was prospectively registered. It stops there. Nothing captures the protocol versions the investigators considered and abandoned during the iterative process that the target trial literature itself describes, so a guideline built from this extraction can only require reporting of the protocol that survived.
problems.quote: Two independent reviewers will extract information on study authors, year of publication, journal, subfield of medicine, study design, sample size, intervention, comparison group, outcomes assessed and whether the study was prospectively registered.

problems.evidence: The stated objective is a minimum set of items reported to give a clear and transparent account of an emulation. Item selection runs through importance ratings and a majority vote, which produces a list of things to state, not a structure that separates assumptions verifiable in the data, such as alignment of eligibility with time zero, from assumptions that no diagnostic can reach, such as no unmeasured confounding or consistency across treatment versions. Both will be reported in the same register.
problems.quote: The objective of the TARGET guideline is to provide guidance on the minimum set of items that should be reported to provide a clear and transparent account of observational studies that investigate the comparative effectiveness and safety of health interventions explicitly using the target trial framework.

problems.evidence: The threshold governing what enters the guideline is procedural rather than substantive: a simple majority of an anonymised vote among invited participants decides inclusion or exclusion of a disputed item. That fixes what must be disclosed, not what would count as an adequate emulation, an acceptable level of residual confounding or a sufficient sensitivity analysis, and the guideline is explicitly a reporting instrument rather than an appraisal one.
problems.quote: For the anonymised vote, a simple majority will be sufficient to guide the inclusion/exclusion of an item.
problems.locator: Stage 3: consolidate and prioritise key items

problems.evidence: The review that will define practice commits to publishing its own data and code, but the items it extracts from the emulations it reviews concern the specified and emulated protocol rather than the artifacts a reader would need to reproduce one. Phenotype logic, weight diagnostics, analysis code and rejected protocol versions appear nowhere in the extraction list, so a guideline derived from it inherits that boundary.
problems.quote: Incomplete reporting of these studies limits the ability of clinicians, researchers, patients and other decision-makers to appraise and synthesise findings or interpret them to inform clinical and public health practice and policy.

papers.title: Evaluation of national institute for health and care excellence guidance for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms by emulating a hypothetical target trial.
papers.one_line: A two-centre retrospective series of 298 ruptured aortic aneurysm repairs in which a weighted subcohort of 144 guideline-compliant patients is compared against the whole cohort under the label of a hypothetical target trial, giving risk ratios of 0.88, 0.92 and 0.99.
papers.what_was_done: Records from Leeds between 2007 and 2016 and Vienna between 2000 and 2016 supplied 298 patients treated for ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm, 112 endovascular and 186 open repairs, with 184 deaths observed. Compliance with UK guidance was defined retrospectively from the treatment actually received: women having endovascular repair, men over 70 having endovascular repair, men 70 or under having open repair. This produced 144 compliers, 48.3 percent of the series. The usual care arm is the entire cohort and the compliant arm is a propensity-weighted subcohort of it, weighted on age, sex, diabetes, chronic lung disease, chronic kidney disease and hemodynamic stability. Stability was missing for 32 percent of Leeds cases and so was dropped from that centre's model, and 14 Vienna cases were excluded for missing covariates, leaving 284 for comparison. Weighted Kaplan-Meier survival under compliance was 73.1 percent at 30 days, 60.2 percent at one year and 42.9 percent at five years against 69.2, 56.5 and 42.4 percent under usual care, with risk ratios of 0.88 with 95 percent CI 0.67 to 1.09, 0.92 with 0.76 to 1.08 and 0.99 with 0.87 to 1.12. Graft configuration and material were left to operator discretion.

future_research.gap: The drivers of the poor long-term survival seen in both arms are unidentified
future_research.quote: Understanding the factors that contribute to these poor long-term outcomes represent an important area for future study.

future_research.gap: Whether the guidance strategy is optimal for older patients is not settled by the comparison, which showed no long-term difference
future_research.quote: Further studies are required in this area to build the evidence base that this is indeed the optimal approach for patients.

problems.evidence: The design compares a cohort against a reweighted subset of itself: 144 compliers drawn from the same 298 patients whose outcomes also constitute the usual care arm. The word emulation is doing the work that an assumption argument would otherwise have to do, since no exchangeability condition is stated for a contrast in which every complier appears on both sides, and the risk ratios of 0.88, 0.92 and 0.99 are reported and interpreted as guideline evidence with no accounting for the induced dependency beyond a bootstrap that accommodates it.
problems.quote: The outcome under usual care can be estimated from our total study cohort, and the sub-cohort of NICE-compliers serves as the basis to estimate the outcome if all patients were treated compliant to NICE.

problems.evidence: The intervention is compliance with a guideline, which is a policy addressed to clinicians rather than a treatment given to patients, and its emulated version is defined entirely by the procedure a patient received in combination with sex and age. Nothing states what a clinician assigned to the compliance strategy would do when anatomy or hemodynamics rule out the recommended procedure, and the paper elsewhere records that treatment decisions depended on device instructions for use, local expertise and service availability, none of which enters the strategy definition.
problems.quote: Female patients, male patients older than 70 years with rEVAR, and male patients up to 70 years of age with rOSR were considered as NICE-compliers.
problems.locator: Definition of compliers of NICE criteria and modified NICE criteria

problems.evidence: Within the endovascular arm, bifurcated against aorto-uni-iliac configuration with femorofemoral bypass is left to the operating team, and within the open arm, graft material and the level of proximal aortic control are left to the surgeon. Two patients recorded as receiving the same strategy may therefore have received procedures with different mortality profiles across 298 patients and 184 deaths, and no argument establishes that these versions form one equivalence class for 30-day or five-year survival.
problems.quote: The decision to perform rEVAR with a bifurcated graft or aorto-uni-iliac configuration in conjunction with a femoro- femoral bypass was left to the discretion of the operating team.

problems.evidence: The two contributing centres do not support the same emulation. Hemodynamic stability, the variable that defines the modified compliance strategy, was missing for 32 percent of Leeds cases, so it was dropped from that centre's propensity model while retained in Vienna's, and the entire modified analysis excludes Leeds. The pooled risk ratios therefore average one centre's weighted comparison adjusted for stability with another's that is not, and the sites differ also in recruitment window, 2007 to 2016 against 2000 to 2016.
problems.quote: Patients of center 1 were excluded from this sub-analysis due to the large number of missing values in the baseline variable stability.

problems.evidence: Weights are the inverted predicted probabilities of compliance from a six-variable logistic model, and the compliant subcohort is nested inside the comparison cohort by construction, so patients with a low modelled probability of compliance receive large weights while contributing to both arms. The reported output is the weighted survival curve and risk ratios; nothing names which combinations of age, sex, comorbidity and stability had no compliant counterpart, and the subgroup analyses in women, men 70 or under and men over 70 rest on as few as 19 compliant patients.
problems.quote: This method was used to account for the special dependency-structure of the two cohorts

problems.evidence: Residual confounding is acknowledged in a closing sentence and left there. The determinants of treatment choice that the paper itself names, anatomical suitability for endovascular repair and hemodynamic status on arrival, are either unmeasured or missing for a third of one centre, and aneurysm morphology was assessable for only 102 and 104 patients. No negative control outcome, no proxy for anatomical suitability and no validation subsample is brought to bear on the risk ratios of 0.88 to 0.99.
problems.quote: As with all retrospective patient cohorts the possibility of residual confounding which cannot be factored in the analysis must be considered.

papers.title: Defining the role of real-world data in cancer clinical research: The position of the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer.
papers.one_line: An institutional position paper that assigns study designs to research questions by a four-factor rubric, places observational target trial emulation last in that ordering and specifies its requirements as aligned time zero plus confounder adjustment as much as possible.
papers.what_was_done: A cooperative oncology group with more than 1400 completed studies sets out a strategy for real-world data. The dichotomy between randomized and real-world evidence is rejected on the grounds that pragmatic trials and cohort multiple randomized trials generate both, and a hybrid category is defined for this combination. Study design is to be selected by four factors: whether a population-level dataset or a subset suffices, whether data collection predates study design, whether treatment delivery must be controlled, and whether the study tests or generates hypotheses. A table maps seven exemplar questions onto designs; comparative effectiveness questions are assigned to a randomized trial or a hybrid design, while questions answered by observational real-world data are classed as hypothesis-generating and exploratory. Observational analyses following the target trial principle are reserved for situations where randomization is not feasible, and their requirements are stated as two: time zero coinciding with eligibility determination and intervention assignment, and confounder adjustment as far as possible. The limits named for registry data include absent detail on toxicities and comorbidities. No numeric threshold, diagnostic or acceptance criterion appears anywhere in the strategy.

future_research.gap: When equipoise has disappeared, randomized evidence cannot be generated and the position paper leaves no design able to supply confirmatory evidence
future_research.quote: It may not be possible though to deliver such evidence in situations where equipoise is no longer present and randomisation would therefore not be feasible
future_research.locator: Defining the scope of applicability of RWD and R²WD

problems.evidence: An organisation that has run more than 1400 trials commits to observational emulation in defined circumstances and states the standard as confounders adjusted for as much as possible. That is a direction of effort, not a threshold: nothing states how much residual confounding is acceptable, what sensitivity analysis would suffice, or what would cause an emulation to be rejected. The parallel commitment to work exclusively with high-quality and auditable real-world data carries no definition of either adjective.
problems.quote: In situations where randomisation cannot be implemented for practical or ethical reasons, the organisation will consider setting up non-randomised RWD studies adhering to the target trial principle, if circumstances permit.

problems.evidence: Two requirements are placed on an emulation: alignment of time zero with eligibility and assignment, which is checkable in the data, and confounder adjustment as far as possible, which is not. They are stated as one pair with the same weight, so a reader cannot tell that the first can be verified and the second cannot. No third category of assumption, such as consistency across treatment versions or absence of interference, is mentioned at all.
problems.quote: there are no guarantees that all of these factors will be identified and measured
problems.locator: RWD versus RCT-derived data: a false dichotomy

problems.evidence: Design class rather than assumption burden determines evidential standing throughout: observational real-world analyses are declared unsuitable for comparative effectiveness against standard of care and are tabulated as hypothesis-generating, while a hybrid randomized design is confirmatory by category. An emulation with a well-supported positivity region and validated phenotypes gets the same classification as one without, and no criterion is offered by which a particular emulation could earn a different status.
problems.quote: they may not be appropriate for assessing the effectiveness of these treatments relative to established standards of care
problems.locator: Defining the scope of applicability of RWD and R²WD

problems.evidence: The fitness argument is narrative from beginning to end: registries are said not to record toxicities or comorbidities in detail, data collected only to support care may be of insufficient evidentiary value, and the organisation will work exclusively with high-quality and auditable data. Insufficient, high-quality and auditable are each left undefined, so no assessment could ever conclude that a specific oncology registry falls below the line and stop a study.
problems.quote: many registries, unlike RCT-linked databases, do not record in detail the toxicities experienced by the individuals whose data they capture, nor the comorbidities these people suffer from
problems.locator: RWD versus RCT-derived data: a false dichotomy

problems.evidence: The stated reason for preferring randomization is that no guarantee exists that all confounders will be identified and measured, which is precisely the situation negative controls, proxies and validation data exist to interrogate. None of them appears in the strategy. The response to unmeasured confounding is to change design rather than to bring evidence about the assumption, so an emulation undertaken when randomization is infeasible carries no workflow for bounding what adjustment missed.
problems.quote: they may be of insufficient evidentiary value to deliver actionable RWE
problems.locator: RWD versus RCT-derived data: a false dichotomy

papers.title: Emulating a target trial of intensive nurse home visiting in the policy-relevant population using linked administrative data.
papers.one_line: A target trial of a South Australian nurse home visiting programme emulated in whole-of-population linked administrative data, where the headline reading benefit of minus 20.6 percentage points under TMLE disappeared under g-computation, inverse probability weighting and the overlapping sample.
papers.what_was_done: The Better Evidence Better Outcomes Linked Data platform supplied whole-of-population South Australian records linked across birth registration, perinatal, public housing, child protection, education and child development sources. Analytical samples were 45 150 children for the developmental census outcome and 61 185 for the literacy and numeracy outcome; 12 percent of newborns were programme-eligible, and the intervention arm comprised 2025 and 2381 children who received an offer and at least one visit against control arms of 2135 and 3989 eligible children who received neither. Adjustment covered 29 confounders using targeted maximum likelihood estimation with SuperLearner, with missing covariates handled by the missing covariate indicator method. Over 40 percent of records in each arm had at least one incomplete covariate and missing outcome proportions were high, with private-school literacy results not available for linkage. The primary analysis estimated an increase in developmental vulnerability of 7.4 percentage points with 95 percent CI 4.8 to 10.0 and a reduction in below-standard reading of minus 20.6 percentage points with 95 percent CI minus 23.5 to minus 17.7, but all eight combinations of three estimators and four missing-data methods were reported and the beneficial estimates vanished outside TMLE on the main sample. Period-specific analyses showed the effect moving from beneficial to adverse across birth cohorts.

future_research.gap: Missing outcomes for private-school children cannot be recovered by any missing-data method available
future_research.quote: but the lack of linkage to NAPLAN results for private schools would remain a threat to the "recoverability" of the effect

future_research.gap: Dose-response per-protocol effects cannot be estimated because reasons for leaving the programme were never recorded
future_research.quote: Other possible per protocol effects could examine the effect of receiving a larger number of visits, but estimation of those effects would require data, such as reasons for dropping out of the programme, that were not available for this study.

problems.evidence: The target trial defines its population by two criteria, one of which is that a family would accept the offer if made. Acceptance is not recorded anywhere, so receipt of at least one visit is used as its proxy under an assumption that the two coincide among those offered. The eligible population is thus defined by what the data recorded rather than by the protocol: 2025 of 5300 eligible newborns for the developmental outcome, selected on a post-offer behavior, and the estimand becomes an average effect in the treated rather than the policy-relevant population effect specified.
problems.quote: However, we did not have a binary indicator D identifying those who would in addition accept an offer, which would be needed to emulate eligibility Criterion (b).

problems.evidence: This does what the entry asks and shows that estimator choice mattered: all eight combinations of three estimators and four missing-data methods are reported side by side, and a minus 20.6 percentage point reading benefit under TMLE with the missing covariate indicator method collapses toward zero under g-computation, inverse probability weighting and the overlapping sample. What stays open is adjudication. No criterion selects among the eight, TMLE is designated primary in advance without a rule that would have preferred it, and the substantive conclusion of no robust effect is reached by inspecting the spread rather than by a defined decision procedure.
problems.quote: However, in the common sample or considering other estimation methods, these beneficial effect estimates disappeared.

problems.evidence: Nuisance models for outcome, arm and missingness are fitted with SuperLearner, an ensemble tuned by cross-validated prediction error, and the resulting TMLE intervals are the narrowest of the eight analyses while also carrying the only large effects. The paper notes that TMLE robustness to misspecification does not extend to standard errors and that bias in them has been observed at comparable sample sizes, so prediction-optimal nuisance fitting delivers estimates that neither replicate under other estimators nor carry trustworthy uncertainty.
problems.quote: Whereas TMLE is robust to mis-specification in terms of parameter estimates, this robustness does not extend to standard error and confidence interval estimation, with bias having been observed in similar sample sizes.

problems.evidence: Outcome missingness is high and differential, since literacy results for private-school children are never linked, and over 40 percent of records in each arm have at least one incomplete covariate. Missingness is treated as a nuisance to model, through a missing covariate indicator in the nuisance regressions and a missingness model inside TMLE, yet the paper concedes the private-school gap threatens recoverability outright. Whether a child appears in the education data at all is a consequence of school-sector choice, itself linked to the disadvantage that defines eligibility.
problems.quote: Proportions of missing outcome data were high and unadjusted risk estimates based on available data were higher in the intervention arm than control arm

problems.evidence: The programme runs to 34 visits over two years on a tapering schedule across six modules, and the emulated intervention is receipt of at least one visit. A family visited once and a family visited 34 times occupy the same arm, and the paper states that dose-specific per-protocol effects would need data on reasons for leaving the programme which were never collected. Heterogeneity across delivery centres is separately identified as the only measured characteristic that differed across birth cohorts, so version variation is both present and unmodeled.
problems.quote: The target trial defines the causal effect of interest as the effect of receiving at least one visit, which would correspond to a type of per protocol effect in a real trial.

problems.evidence: The whole design exists to reach a policy-relevant population that trials cannot enrol, and it does so by stacking a representativeness assumption on top of the confounding assumptions: offer receipt must be independent of the 29 covariates given service area and remoteness, and receipt of a visit must equal acceptance among those offered. Those sampling assumptions are stated in a causal diagram and never probed, while the arms differ sharply on the covariates in question, with median maternal age 22 to 23 against 28 to 29 years and Indigenous proportions of 23.1 percent against 10.9 to 14.8 percent.
problems.quote: It can be difficult for RCTs to enrol the populations that are of policy relevance,
